meta.title: Present Continuous Tenses Test - Gen Z Themes
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering English Present Continuous Tenses.
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined grammar structures involving the Present Continuous tense paired with topics like gerunds, relative clauses, passive voice, quantifiers, prepositions, and more, all within familiar Gen Z contexts.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: I am currently considering _____ a Twitch channel, so I am _____ speaking to my camera every day.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. 'Consider' is followed by a gerund ('starting'), and 'am practicing' is the correct Present Continuous form.
explanation.concept: Verbs requiring gerund complements in Present Continuous contexts
explanation.formula: Subject + am/is/are + considering + verb-ing; subject + am/is/are + verb-ing
examples: I am considering moving, so I am practicing my new language.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with quantifiers and verb patterns. 'Clothes' is plural, requiring 'are'. 'Shoppers' is countable, requiring 'a few'. 'Try' is followed by a to-infinitive ('to find').
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement, countable quantifiers, and infinitive patterns
explanation.formula: Many of + plural noun + are + verb-ing; a few of + plural noun + are + trying to + base verb
examples: Many of the items are selling, and a few of the buyers are trying to find deals.

data.hint: Choose the correct prepositions to complete the sentence.
data.question: She is currently focusing _____ her mental health and is talking _____ a therapist about her anxiety.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with preposition collocations. 'Focusing' is followed by 'on', and 'talking' (in this context) is followed by 'to'.
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after specific verbs
explanation.formula: Am/is/are focusing on + noun; am/is/are talking to + noun
examples: He is focusing on his goals and talking to his mentor.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with non-defining relative clauses. The plural subject 'idols' requires the plural auxiliary 'are'. 'Records' is plural and does not take 'a'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement in plural relative clauses
explanation.formula: Plural noun, who + are + verb-ing, + are + verb-ing + plural noun
examples: The artists, who are currently touring, are breaking records.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: My roommate _____ always _____ their dirty dishes in the sink while I am trying to cook.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with adverbs of frequency to express annoyance. 'Is always leaving' is the correct structure for a recurring, irritating action.
explanation.concept: Using 'always' with Present Continuous for annoyance
explanation.formula: Subject + am/is/are + always + verb-ing
examples: He is always interrupting me during meetings.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous passive voice with subject-verb agreement. 'Update' is singular, requiring 'is'. 'Players' is plural, requiring 'are'. 'To be' is the correct infinitive form.
explanation.topic: Present Continuous + Passive Voice + Subject-Verb Agreement
explanation.concept: Singular and plural agreement in Present Continuous passive
explanation.formula: Singular subject + is being + past participle; plural subject + are + expecting + to be + past participle
examples: The app is being updated, and users are expecting it to be fixed.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: We _____ the music festival next weekend, so we _____ our outfits right now.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense for future arrangements with the Present Continuous for actions happening right now.
explanation.topic: Present Continuous (Future Arrangements) + Present Continuous (Current Actions)
explanation.concept: Using Present Continuous for fixed future plans and current actions
explanation.formula: Subject + am/is/are + verb-ing (future) + , so + subject + am/is/are + verb-ing (now)
examples: We are meeting tomorrow, so we are preparing today.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with phrasal verbs and verb patterns. 'Am trying' is the correct continuous form. 'Try to' is followed by the base verb ('cut'). 'Am studying' is the correct continuous form.
explanation.topic: Present Continuous + Phrasal Verbs + Verb Patterns
explanation.concept: Correct verb forms in continuous and infinitive structures
explanation.formula: Subject + am/is/are + trying + to + base verb; subject + am/is/are + verb-ing
examples: I am trying to eat healthier while I am working out.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Sustainable fashion _____ more popular than fast fashion, and brands _____ their strategies accordingly.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with advanced comparatives. 'Is becoming' shows a current trend, and 'are adapting' shows an ongoing action.
explanation.concept: Describing current trends and ongoing adaptations
explanation.formula: Subject + is/are + becoming + more + adjective + than + noun; subject + are + verb-ing
examples: Electric cars are becoming cheaper, and companies are adapting quickly.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with modal verbs of deduction. 'Can't be playing' is the correct modal continuous form. 'Supposed to be' is the correct adjective phrase, followed by the continuous 'preparing'.
explanation.concept: Modal continuous for deduction and 'supposed to be' + verb-ing
explanation.formula: Subject + can't be + verb-ing; subject + is supposed to be + verb-ing
examples: She can't be sleeping; she is supposed to be studying.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: While I _____ my vlog, my friend _____ the best hashtags to use.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with conjunctions of time. 'While' + Present Continuous sets the background action, and the main clause uses Present Continuous for a simultaneous action.
explanation.concept: Parallel actions in progress at the same time
explanation.formula: While + subject + am/is/are + verb-ing, subject + am/is/are + verb-ing
examples: While I am cooking, she is setting the table.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with ellipsis and subject-verb agreement. 'Am binge-watching' and 'is doing' are the correct continuous forms. 'We' requires the plural auxiliary 'are'.
explanation.concept: Correct continuous forms and plural agreement
explanation.formula: Subject + am/is/are + verb-ing; plural subject + are + verb-ing
examples: I am reading, and he is doing the same while we are resting.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Currently, many young activists _____ for climate action; nevertheless, some politicians _____ their demands.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with discourse markers. 'Are protesting' and 'are ignoring' describe ongoing current actions, contrasted by 'nevertheless'.
explanation.concept: Describing ongoing actions with contrastive markers
explanation.formula: Currently, subject + are + verb-ing; nevertheless, subject + are + verb-ing
examples: People are demanding change; nevertheless, leaders are delaying action.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. 'Trying to avoid' is the correct infinitive pattern. 'Am enjoying' is the correct continuous form. 'Of' is followed by a gerund ('scrolling').
explanation.concept: Verbs and prepositions requiring gerund complements
explanation.formula: Am/is/are trying to avoid + verb-ing; am/is/are enjoying + verb-ing; of + verb-ing
examples: I am trying to avoid eating sugar, and I am enjoying drinking water instead of consuming soda.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: If the algorithm _____ my video right now, I will get more views by tomorrow.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with First Conditionals. 'Is pushing' describes an action happening right now that serves as the condition for a future result.
explanation.concept: Present Continuous in 'if' clauses for current ongoing conditions
explanation.formula: If + subject + am/is/are + verb-ing, subject + will + base verb
examples: If it is raining now, we will stay inside.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with article usage and subject-verb agreement. 'Unique' starts with a consonant sound (/j/), requiring 'a'. 'She' requires 'is'. 'A specific' requires the singular 'palette'.
explanation.concept: Indefinite articles before consonant sounds and singular agreement
explanation.formula: Subject + is + creating + a + word starting with /j/ sound; subject + is + choosing + a + singular noun
examples: He is designing a unique logo, and he is choosing a specific color.

data.hint: Choose the correct prepositions to complete the sentence.
data.question: He is currently interested _____ learning how to code, and he is good _____ solving logic puzzles.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with preposition collocations. 'Interested' is followed by 'in', and 'good' is followed by 'at'.
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after specific adjectives
explanation.formula: Am/is/are interested in + verb-ing; am/is/are good at + verb-ing
examples: She is interested in painting and good at drawing.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with cleft sentences. 'It is' is required for singular emphasis. 'Crowd' is a collective noun treated as singular here, requiring 'is'. 'Energy' is uncountable and does not take 's'.
explanation.concept: Subject-verb agreement and uncountable nouns in cleft structures
explanation.formula: It + is + singular noun + who/that + is + verb-ing; singular collective noun + is + verb-ing + uncountable noun
examples: It is the chef who is cooking, and the audience is loving the energy.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: The anime that _____ currently _____ on streaming platforms is getting a lot of attention from fans.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with relative clauses. The singular subject 'anime' requires the singular auxiliary 'is' and the present participle 'airing'.
explanation.concept: Singular agreement in relative clauses using Present Continuous
explanation.formula: Singular noun + that + is + verb-ing + is + verb-ing
examples: The show that is currently airing is getting praise.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous passive with quantifiers and subject-verb agreement. 'Brands' is plural, requiring 'are'. 'Waste' is uncountable, requiring 'is'. 'Companies' is plural, requiring 'these'.
explanation.concept: Plural and uncountable agreement in Present Continuous
explanation.formula: Many of + plural noun + are + verb-ing; much of + uncountable noun + is + being + past participle; these + plural noun
examples: Many of the stores are opening, and much of the trash is being recycled by these groups.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: When I _____ to Japan next month, I _____ all the major anime studios.

B.text: am traveling / am going to visit

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense for future arrangements with 'be going to' for future intentions. 'Am traveling' is the fixed plan, and 'am going to visit' is the intention.
explanation.concept: Future arrangements and intentions in time clauses
explanation.formula: When + subject + am/is/are + verb-ing, subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb
examples: When I am flying tomorrow, I am going to read a book.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with separable phrasal verbs and modal verb patterns. 'Plugging it in' is the correct pronoun placement. 'Can' is followed by the base verb 'start'. 'Start' is followed by the gerund 'playing'.
explanation.topic: Present Continuous + Phrasal Verbs + Modal Verbs
explanation.concept: Pronoun placement in phrasal verbs and base verb after modals
explanation.formula: Subject + am/is/are + verb + pronoun + particle; modal + base verb + verb-ing
examples: I am turning it on, so we can start working.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: I am currently _____ trying out new vegan recipes, and I am _____ washing the dishes afterward.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. 'Am enjoying' and 'am dreading' are the correct continuous forms, both followed by gerunds ('trying', 'washing').
explanation.concept: Continuous forms of emotion verbs followed by gerunds
explanation.formula: Am/is/are + enjoying/dreading + verb-ing
examples: I am loving eating this, and I am hating cleaning up.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with subject-verb agreement. 'Community' is a collective noun treated as singular here, requiring 'is'. 'Developers' is plural, requiring 'are'. 'Fix' is singular and does not take 's'.
explanation.concept: Collective singular and plural agreement
explanation.formula: Singular collective noun + is + verb-ing; plural noun + are + verb-ing + singular noun
examples: The team is practicing, and the coaches are planning a fix.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: She _____ the new dance routine flawlessly right now, and her followers _____ her progress closely.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with adverbs of manner. 'Is currently practicing' and 'are watching' describe actions happening at the moment of speaking.
explanation.concept: Describing current actions and how they are performed
explanation.formula: Subject + is/are + currently + verb-ing + adverb; subject + are + verb-ing + adverb
examples: He is currently playing well, and we are watching closely.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with preposition collocations. 'Relying' and 'depending' are both followed by 'on'. 'A stable' requires the singular 'connection'.
explanation.concept: Correct preposition usage after specific verbs
explanation.formula: Am/is/are relying on + noun; am/is/are depending on + singular noun

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: As the semester _____ more demanding, students _____ out more study groups.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with conjunctions of time. 'Is getting' and 'are seeking' describe changing situations and ongoing actions happening around the present time.
explanation.concept: Describing changing situations with 'as'
explanation.formula: As + subject + is/are + verb-ing, subject + is/are + verb-ing
examples: As the weather is getting colder, people are buying more coats.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous passive with relative clauses. 'Jackets' is plural, requiring 'are being' and 'are becoming'. 'At this' requires the singular 'moment'.
explanation.topic: Present Continuous + Relative Clauses + Passive Voice
explanation.concept: Plural agreement in passive relative clauses
explanation.formula: Plural noun, which + are being + past participle, + are + verb-ing + at this + singular noun
examples: The shoes, which are being sold, are popular at this moment.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: We _____ at the coffee shop at 3 PM, and we _____ the group project then.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense for future arrangements. 'Are meeting' and 'are discussing' describe fixed plans for a specific future time.
explanation.concept: Using Present Continuous for fixed future plans
explanation.formula: Subject + am/is/are + verb-ing (future time) + , and + subject + am/is/are + verb-ing (future time)
examples: We are having dinner at 7, and we are watching a movie then.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Present Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. 'Considering' and 'suggesting' must both be followed by a gerund ('moving', 'looking'), not a to-infinitive.
explanation.concept: Verbs requiring gerund complements in Present Continuous
explanation.formula: Am/is/are + considering/suggesting + verb-ing
examples: I am considering changing jobs, and they are suggesting applying online.
